candidate_sentences.text: During the financial year ended 31 December 2025, AS Merko Ehitus group reported revenue of 310.9 million euros, representing a decrease of 42.3 percent compared to 539.0 million euros in 2024.
Gross profit for 2025 stood at 55.9 million euros compared to 95.9 million euros in 2024, with a stable gross margin of 18.0 percent against 17.8 percent previously.
Operating profit for the reporting period was 34.3 million euros, down from 72.5 million euros, yielding an operating profit margin of 11.0 percent compared to 13.4 percent.
Net profit attributable to equity holders of the parent was 39.9 million euros, down from 64.7 million euros, while the net margin improved to 12.8 percent from 12.0 percent.

verified_key_information_units.information: The 2025 revenue decline was driven by the completion of major projects initiated in prior years during 2025, combined with a slower pace of new contract signing in 2024 and the first half of 2025; this project cycle effect compressed profitability despite eventual improvement in contract signing activity later in 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'In 2024, we were engaged in several large projects that had been started in earlier years, and these were completed as planned during 2025. The pace of signing new contracts was slower in 2024 and in the first half of 2025.'

verified_key_information_units.information: A major improvement in contract signing during the second half of 2025 resulted in the execution of Merko's largest-ever contracts for the Rūdninkai defence campus in Lithuania, which will contribute gradually to revenue starting in 2026 and provide stable workload for years ahead.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company expanded its public-private partnership (PPP) business through new real estate development agreements signed in 2025 for the Krulli quarter (Tallinn) and Uus-Karlowa quarter (Tartu), alongside continued success in the Noblessner area, enhancing long-term workload stability and diversification.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'Alongside the successful real estate development partnership in the Noblessner area of Tallinn, we signed two similar cooperation agreements in 2025 for the development of the Krulli quarter in Tallinn and the Uus-Karlowa quarter in Tartu. The Rūdninkai project marks a significant expansion of our PPP business Lithuania.'

These omissions are material because they represent key drivers of future revenue, workload stability, and profit contributions described in the fixed criteria.
